evidence: You can take a loop by following the North South Track, Waipapa Track/Crimson Thread Track and Waiorongomai Valley tracks. It is 4-5 hours from the junction with the North South Track, taking this loop option.
From the junction of the Pylon Peak Summit Track and the North South Track, take the left-hand branch of the North South Track and follow it along the Kaimai range (towards Mt Te Aroha).

From the saddle, turn off the ridge and descend into Waiorongomai Valley on the Te Aroha Link track. Follow the signposts to return back to the car park (there are various track options through Waiorongomai Valley).

doubts: The page is named 'Summit Loop' and DOC's summary gives '4.4 km to the summit' and '13.7 km loop'. The text presents the return-the-same-way summit walk as the main walk and the loop as an 'alternative (more advanced and longer option)', so the out-and-back is main and the loop is W2. DOC's '6-7 hr' is not tied in the text to either way, so both times are null. The main way turns at the junction with the North South Track, which the text reaches after around 2 hour 30 min; the text does not call it the summit, so it is not recorded as one. The loop is recorded from the car park, although the text describes it from the junction. The Pylon Peak Summit Track is matched to the map track 'Pylon Peak Track' (T2) by name. The Low-Level Track has no map entry (the feature is 'Low Level Drive Track'). The unnamed stream crossed after the signposted junction is not listed.
